coordinates.locator: OSM D0 Assembly Building centroid (extract of 2026-09-18)
coordinates.note: The D0 assembly/collision hall building is mapped in OpenStreetMap; the coordinate is the building centroid, within about 40 m of the hall. It is shown as approximate because OpenStreetMap is a community map and not a survey; the 40 m precision is the half-size of the footprint. It replaces a Fermilab campus point of 3 km precision.

name: D0 collision hall (Tevatron D0)
notes: The point is the centroid of the D0 Assembly Building as mapped in OpenStreetMap (see the coordinate note). No survey or official source consulted gives a dedicated lat/lon for this interaction hall.

fnal.gov states "DZero is one of two detectors positioned along the four-mile Tevatron accelerator ring. It takes its name from its location on the ring, D0." (src:colliders-historical-d0-fnal-tevatron-experiments-page), confirming the D0 location name, though not coordinates.

summary.plain: The interaction hall on the Fermilab Tevatron ring where the D0 detector sat, in Batavia, Illinois. Its position is the centroid of the hall building as traced in OpenStreetMap, not a surveyed point.
summary.technical: D0 collision hall (Tevatron D0): one of the Tevatron ring's interaction regions, at Fermilab, Batavia, Illinois. No survey coordinate for the hall itself was found; the marker is the centroid of the hall building as mapped in OpenStreetMap (about 40 m), shown as approximate.
